BLOCKER: Language rule: `core/execution_trail.py` (show) gaining new render logic is new shipped logic in Python; design does not state whether this is an "edit to shipped Python" vs new logic, and no Go placement is proposed. AC claims language-rule checks pass but the design contradicts it.

No decided policy for pre-existing completed items lacking `ac_verification`/`final_report`: "backfill or grandfathering" is left open. An undecided completion-guard behavior is an unfalsifiable invariant — pick one, list the affected ids, and test it.
MAJOR: Enforcement is spread across `gate1_check.py`, `gate_decisions.py`, `execution_trail_check.py`, and `disposition_policy.py`; design does not name a single writer/owner for disposition+AC policy. CL-001 route-by-kind requires one module that all gates call, else the cap/approval rules will drift per gate.

Finding signature (`finding sigs`) algorithm and stability invariant are unstated: if sigs hash volatile fields (timestamps, ordering, wording), approvals break on re-render or become forgeable by trivial edits. Define the sig inputs and add a tamper/round-trip test.

ACCEPTED cap is "per review mode" but the aggregate behavior (e.g., 2 design + 2 diff = 4 accepted per item) is unspecified; state whether caps are independent or item-global and test the combined case.

`finalize_item.py` persistence has no stated atomicity/single-writer contract: partial writes or concurrent finalize runs could leave a half-populated `final_report` that passes merge checks. Require write-then-rename (or equivalent) plus an idempotency invariant.
DEFERRED "cites an existing backlog id" needs an existence check against the store at each gate, and a rule for ids later closed/deleted; otherwise the cite degrades to a free-text string.
MINOR: DEFERRED id validation, cost_source enumeration (allowed values, required-when-cost-present), and test-kind taxonomy (`other` catch-all) need documented rules; add invariant test that per-kind counts/durations sum to the reported totals.
Guardrail refusals (cap exceeded, missing approval, failed AC, missing final report) emit no stated log/metric; observability gap will make gate failures hard to diagnose in CI.
No explicit test that Gate 2.5 flagging an AC gap does *not* certify it (the "2.5 may flag but not certify" negative case).
Rollback note says "revert the commit" but post-revert orphan fields (`final_report`, `ac_verification`) in stored items are unaddressed; confirm read paths tolerate unknown/extra fields.
NIT: `config/review-dispositions.json` ownership/updater not named (who edits caps/config vs code); add to store-registry docs to prevent config drift.
Recurring `_render_review`/`_item_dispositions` test gap from prior reviews should be explicitly added to the test list to avoid a third repeat.
SUMMARY: Verdict: conceptually sound and well-scoped (guards at Gate 1/2/completion, persisted report, docs), but two items must be settled before Gate 1.5: the language-rule placement of new `show` rendering logic, and the grandfathering-vs-backfill decision for existing items.
Top risks: enforcement logic duplicated across gate scripts without a named single writer; unspecified finding-signature stability; non-atomic final_report persistence.
